alert.title: Atypical travel
alert.description: Sign-in from Paris then Amsterdam within 40 minutes.

arguments.query: SigninLogs | where UserPrincipalName =~ "jdoe@contoso.com" | where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-09-14T08:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-09-14T11:00:00Z)) | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, City, ResultType, AppDisplayName, ClientAppUsed, DeviceDetail | order by TimeGenerated asc

arguments.query: atypical travel alert same IP different city SASE geolocation false positive

hits.title: Atypical travel: known egress points
hits.excerpt: The group SASE gateways egress from 203.0.113.0/24 (Amsterdam) and 198.51.100.0/24 (Paris). A sign-in pair inside these ranges within one hour is a gateway hand-over, not travel.

hits.title: Identity Protection triage checklist
hits.excerpt: Confirm MFA outcome, device compliance, and whether the source IP is a corporate egress before escalating.

redacted_response.detail: no fixture stub for get_asset matches arguments {"asset": "203.0.113.7"}

arguments.recommended_action: Close the alert as false positive referencing RB-0114 (known SASE egress ranges). No user action needed; optionally tune the Identity Protection atypical-travel detection to exclude sign-ins sourced from 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/24 SASE gateway ranges to reduce recurring noise for this and other users behind the same gateway.
arguments.summary: Both sign-ins attributed to "Paris" (09:12 UTC) and "Amsterdam" (09:51 UTC) for jdoe@contoso.com originated from the identical IP address 203.0.113.7, which sits inside the corporate SASE gateway egress range documented in runbook RB-0114 (203.0.113.0/24 = Amsterdam gateway, 198.51.100.0/24 = Paris gateway); the runbook states that a sign-in pair inside these ranges within an hour is a gateway hand-over, not physical travel. Both sign-ins succeeded (ErrorCode 0) with no error, the IP has no malicious VirusTotal signal (0/94, AS owner EXAMPLE-SASE-NET consistent with a SASE provider), and a similar prior alert for this user (Unfamiliar sign-in properties, incident 38) was already closed as a false positive. jdoe is a legitimate employee (Paris-based trader, employed since 2019, not on watchlist), so there is no indication of account compromise; the geolocation discrepancy is an artifact of the SASE gateway's IP-to-city mapping rather than actual atypical travel.

observed_facts.statement: Both flagged sign-ins for jdoe@contoso.com within the 40-minute window originated from the exact same IP address, 203.0.113.7, with the sign-in engine geolocating the first as Paris, FR and the second as Amsterdam, NL; both succeeded (ErrorCode 0).

The IP 203.0.113.7 falls inside the 203.0.113.0/24 range that the SOC runbook documents as a corporate SASE gateway egress point (Amsterdam), paired with 198.51.100.0/24 (Paris); the runbook states such pairs within an hour are gateway hand-overs, not travel.

VirusTotal shows no malicious or suspicious engine detections for 203.0.113.7 (0/94) and attributes it to AS owner EXAMPLE-SASE-NET, consistent with a corporate SASE/network provider rather than an anonymizing or malicious host.
jdoe is a legitimate, long-tenured employee (Equities Trading, employed since 2019-03-04) based in Paris, FR, not flagged on any watchlist.
A prior similar Identity Protection alert for the same account ("Unfamiliar sign-in properties", incident 38) was already investigated and classified as a false positive.

assumptions.statement: The SASE gateway's IP-to-geolocation mapping (Paris vs Amsterdam city labels for the same /24 range) is the actual cause of the discrepancy in this instance, not a coincidental use of a shared NAT IP by two different physical users.
assumptions.why_unverified: No direct device/session token correlation or MFA satisfaction log was available to independently confirm it was the same physical session traversing the gateway rather than two distinct sessions sharing an IP.

missing_context.what: Sign-in risk detail (MFA satisfaction, device compliance/join state, session/token correlation) for the two sign-in events.
missing_context.why_it_matters: Would give definitive confirmation that a single authenticated device/session was routed through the SASE gateway's Paris and Amsterdam edges, fully ruling out any possibility of concurrent use from two different endpoints sharing the NAT IP.
missing_context.how_to_obtain: Query AADSignInEventsBeta/SigninLogs for CorrelationId, DeviceDetail (deviceId, trustType, compliance) and AuthenticationRequirement/MFA result for both events, or check Conditional Access sign-in details in Entra ID portal.

result.recommended_action: Close the alert as false positive referencing RB-0114 (known SASE egress ranges); no user action needed. Recommend tuning the Identity Protection atypical-travel detection to exclude sign-ins sourced from the documented 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/24 SASE gateway ranges to reduce recurring noise for this and other users behind the same gateway.
